The first sentence in the report text is very unclear. This first sentence needs to be changed to a brief introduction namely, "9/11 is one of the oldest and most persistent topics in online conspiracy content ("inside job", "controlled demolition", "false flag"). Platforms and fact-checkers increasingly rely on automatic filters to flag such content". Next, in th sentence, "This study asks whether the text of a full article about the 9/11 attacks reveals if it was published on a conspiracy-oriented or on a mainstream website, and how four methods compare on this task", simply saying four methods is not specific enough, it needs to be changed to machiene learning methods for text recognition.

items.text: I am a little confused about the following sentence "The hypotheses were chosen from the literature and fixed before the final test run; the exact date on which they were written down cannot be shown." - i think we should remove the latter part of the sentence.

I think the four methods that we are using should be explained a little bit better, we need to state what we expect out of them. Also we need to justify better why we explicitly chose these 4 methods. After this we go into the hypothesis. 

- What we expected for the Word Counts: We expect plain word counts to tell the two kinds of website apart better than always guessing mainstream, because the two kinds tend to use different words.

- What we expected for the TF-IDF: Giving rare, telling words more weight than everyday words improves on plain word counts.

- What we expected for the TF-IDF plus extra features: Adding features about certainty and writing style improves the TF-IDF model.

- What we expected for the LLM classifier: We expect a cheap language model with no training to do roughly as well as the trained models, because it has read a great deal of text and can judge how an article is written.

In a later explanation the following was written : "We used logistic regression for every trained model because it is simple and its weights can be read as word lists. We did not try other classifiers, because the question is about features, not which method is best. We did not fine-tune a language model, which needs more data and money than we have. We left out emotion features, because fear and anger are normal in reports on an attack and so tell us little." I think this could be used nicely in the explanation of the 4 methods.
Clear differentiation between executive summary and introduction are needed. no results in the introduction.
